questions.question: In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All fans are brown. Some brown are chairs. Some chairs are plastic. Conclusions: I. Some brown are fans. II. Some chairs are brown. III. No chair is plastic.
questions.questionHtml:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:
All fans are brown.
Some brown are chairs.
Some chairs are plastic.
Conclusions:
I. Some brown are fans.
II. Some chairs are brown.
III. No chair is plastic.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow.
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some brown are fans → Follow (As all fans are brown. As whole fans comes in brown, therefore it is true.)

II. Some chairs are brown → Follow (As some brown are chairs. As brown has some part common with chairs, therefore it is true.)

III. No chair is plastic → Does not follow (As some chairs are plastic. As no statements restricts chairs from being plastic, therefore it is false.)

∴ Here, Only I and II conclusion follow.

questions.question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statements Statements: No river is a mountain. Some rivers are animals. Some birds are mountains. Conclusions: I: No animal is a mountain. II: No river is a bird.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statements

Statements:
No river is a mountain.
Some rivers are animals.
Some birds are mountains.

Conclusions:
I: No animal is a mountain.
II: No river is a bird.
questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. No animal is a mountain → Does not follow (As no river is a mountain and some rivers are animals. As no direct relation is given between animals and mountains, therefore it is false.)

II. No river is a bird → Does not follow (As no river is a mountain and some birds are mountains. As no direct relation is given between river and bird, therefore it is false.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:  2nd number - 1st number × 4 - 1 = 3rd number.

Option 1) (22, 45, 91) ⇒ (45 - 22) × 4 - 1 = 91 ⇒ 23 × 4 - 1 = 91 ⇒ 92 - 1 = 91

91 = 91 (LHS = RHS)

Thus, out of all the options, '(22, 45, 91)' follows the same logic as given.

questions.question: In a certain code language, R + T means ‘R is the sister of T’. R - T means ‘R is the father of T’. R * T means ‘R is the wife of T’. R ÷ T means ‘R is the mother of T’. Based on the above, how is F related to C if A + B – C ÷ D * E – F ÷ G?
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,

R + T means ‘R is the sister of T’.

R - T means ‘R is the father of T’.

R * T means ‘R is the wife of T’.

R ÷ T means ‘R is the mother of T’.

Based on the above, how is F related to C if A + B – C ÷ D * E – F ÷ G?
questions.solution:
Given: A + B – C ÷ D * E – F ÷ G - It means that A is sister of B, B is the father of C,C is the mother of D, D is the wife of E, E is the father of F, F is the mother of G.

 

Thus, F is C's daughter’s daughter or granddaughter.
